mcqs.question: Sound A has an amplitude of 5 cm while Sound B has an amplitude of 2 cm. Which of the following statements correctly compares their loudness?

options.A: Sound A is louder than Sound B because it has a larger amplitude.
options.B: Sound B is louder than Sound A because it has a smaller amplitude.
options.C: Both sounds have the same loudness because loudness depends only on frequency.
options.D: Loudness cannot be compared without knowing the medium.

mcqs.answer: Sound A is louder than Sound B because it has a larger amplitude.
mcqs.explanation: Loudness of a sound is directly related to its amplitude: a larger amplitude means greater displacement of particles, producing a louder sound. Therefore, Sound A with the larger amplitude is perceived as louder. Options B, C, and D are incorrect because they either reverse the relationship, ignore amplitude, or introduce irrelevant factors.

mcqs.question: In a competitive exam, a student is asked: If the frequency of a sound wave is increased, what happens to the pitch of the sound?
mcqs.explanation: Pitch is the perceptual attribute of sound that corresponds to its frequency. A higher frequency means more vibrations per second, which the ear perceives as a higher pitch. Option A is the opposite, while C and D are unrelated to the frequency‑pitch relationship.

mcqs.question: Which of the following best defines the amplitude of a sound wave?

options.A: The number of vibrations per second of the source.
options.B: The maximum displacement of particles from their rest position in the medium.
options.C: The time taken for one complete vibration.
options.D: The speed at which the sound travels through the medium.

mcqs.answer: The maximum displacement of particles from their rest position in the medium.
mcqs.explanation: Amplitude measures how far particles in the medium move from their equilibrium position during a vibration. It is directly related to the energy and loudness of the sound. Options A, C, and D describe frequency, time period, and speed respectively, not amplitude.

mcqs.question: What is the definition of frequency in the context of sound waves?

options.A: The distance between two consecutive compressions.
options.B: The number of vibrations or cycles per second produced by the source.
options.C: The height of the wave crest.
options.D: The time taken for one vibration.

mcqs.answer: The number of vibrations or cycles per second produced by the source.
mcqs.explanation: Frequency (measured in hertz) quantifies how many complete cycles occur each second. It determines the pitch of the sound. Option A refers to wavelength, C to amplitude, and D to time period.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly defines the time period of a sound wave and distinguishes it from frequency?

options.A: Time period is the number of cycles per second; frequency is the time for one cycle.
options.B: Time period is the time taken for one complete vibration; frequency is the number of such vibrations per second.
options.C: Both time period and frequency measure the same property and are interchangeable.
options.D: Time period is measured in hertz, while frequency is measured in seconds.

mcqs.answer: Time period is the time taken for one complete vibration; frequency is the number of such vibrations per second.
mcqs.explanation: Time period (T) is the duration of one cycle, measured in seconds, while frequency (f) is the number of cycles per second, measured in hertz. They are inverses of each other (f = 1/T). Options A, C, and D incorrectly reverse or confuse the definitions and units.

mcqs.question: A tuning fork vibrates at a frequency of 250 Hz. What is the time period of the sound wave produced by the fork?
mcqs.explanation: Time period T = 1/f. For f = 250 Hz, T = 1/250 = 0.004 seconds. The other options correspond to incorrect inverses or misplaced decimal places.

mcqs.question: A speaker A produces a sound with an amplitude of 0.8 m, while speaker B produces a sound with an amplitude of 0.2 m. Which statement correctly describes the perceived loudness of the sounds?

options.A: Sound from speaker A will be perceived as louder because it has a greater amplitude.
options.B: Sound from speaker B will be perceived as louder because lower amplitude means higher intensity.
options.C: Both sounds will be perceived with equal loudness because loudness depends only on frequency.
options.D: Loudness cannot be determined without knowing the speed of sound.

mcqs.answer: Sound from speaker A will be perceived as louder because it has a greater amplitude.
mcqs.explanation: Loudness is directly proportional to the amplitude of the sound wave; a larger amplitude transfers more energy to the ear, producing a louder perception. Option B reverses the relationship, C ignores amplitude, and D introduces an irrelevant factor.

mcqs.question: A violin string is tuned to produce a note of 440 Hz (standard A). If the frequency of the string is halved, what happens to the pitch of the note?

options.A: The pitch becomes one octave lower.
options.B: The pitch becomes one octave higher.
options.C: The pitch remains the same but the volume increases.
options.D: The pitch becomes sharper but stays in the same octave.

mcqs.answer: The pitch becomes one octave lower.
mcqs.explanation: Halving the frequency lowers the pitch by one octave, as each octave corresponds to a doubling or halving of frequency. Therefore, a 220 Hz note (half of 440 Hz) is one octave lower. Options B, C, and D describe incorrect effects of frequency change.
